references.text: The same debate about the identity of the healed man continues in verse 8, where neighbors ask if he is the one who used to sit and beg, and in verse 9, where some confirm it while others deny it.
The first verse in this passage shows the neighbors continuing to ask, 'How were your eyes opened?', while the man confirms his identity in the next verse by speaking about Jesus.
The neighbors further ask, 'Where is he?', showing that the debate over the man's identity and Jesus' role in the healing remains central to the conversation.
Later in the chapter, the man again confirms his identity and testifies about Jesus, even though the Pharisees try to deny the healing, paralleling the initial doubt in verse 9.
